L 
L Benchmarks accept options that may be specified either through their command line interface or by setting environment variables before execution. For every `--option_flag=<value>` CLI switch, a corresponding environment variable `OPTION_FLAG=<value>` exists and is used as default if set (CLI switches always prevail).

L <a name="runtime-and-reporting-considerations" />
T 49 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L 
L ## Runtime and Reporting Considerations
T 2 text.html.markdown markup.heading.markdown heading.2.markdown punctuation.definition.heading.markdown
T 3 text.html.markdown markup.heading.markdown heading.2.markdown
T 39 text.html.markdown markup.heading.markdown heading.2.markdown entity.name.section.markdown
L 
L When the benchmark binary is executed, each benchmark function is run serially.
T 79 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L The number of iterations to run is determined dynamically by running the
T 72 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L benchmark a few times and measuring the time taken and ensuring that the
T 72 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L ultimate result will be statistically stable. As such, faster benchmark
T 71 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L functions will be run for more iterations than slower benchmark functions, and
T 78 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L the number of iterations is thus reported.
T 42 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L 
L In all cases, the number of iterations for which the benchmark is run is
T 72 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L governed by the amount of time the benchmark takes. Concretely, the number of
T 77 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L iterations is at least one, not more than 1e9, until CPU time is greater than
T 77 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L the minimum time, or the wallclock time is 5x minimum time. The minimum time is
T 79 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L set per benchmark by calling `MinTime` on the registered benchmark object.
T 29 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
T 30 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown punctuation.definition.raw.markdown
T 37 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown
T 38 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown punctuation.definition.raw.markdown
T 74 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L

T 60 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown

T 1 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown punctuation.definition.raw.markdown

L forms:
T 6 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L 
L * `--benchmark_min_time=<float>s` sets the minimum running time for each

T 72 text.html.markdown markup.list.unnumbered.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L   benchmark repetition in seconds.
T 2 text.html.markdown markup.list.unnumbered.markdown

T 1 text.html.markdown markup.list.unnumbered.markdown punctuation.definition.list.begin.markdown

L 
L In a multithreaded test (benchmark invoked by multiple threads simultaneously),
T 79 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L it is guaranteed that none of the threads will start until all have reached
T 75 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L the start of the benchmark loop, and all will have finished before any thread
T 77 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L exits the benchmark loop. (This behavior is also provided by the `KeepRunning()`
T 65 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
T 66 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown punctuation.definition.raw.markdown
T 79 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown
T 80 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown punctuation.definition.raw.markdown
L API) As such, any global setup or teardown can be wrapped in a check against the thread
T 87 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown

L ## Exiting with an Error

T 3 text.html.markdown markup.heading.markdown heading.2.markdown

L 
L When errors caused by external influences, such as file I/O and network
T 71 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L communication, occur within a benchmark the
T 43 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L `State::SkipWithError(const std::string& msg)` function can be used to skip that run
T 1 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown punctuation.definition.raw.markdown
T 45 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown
T 46 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown punctuation.definition.raw.markdown
T 84 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L of benchmark and report the error. Note that only future iterations of the
T 74 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L `KeepRunning()` are skipped. For the ranged-for version of the benchmark loop
T 1 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown punctuation.definition.raw.markdown
T 14 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown
T 15 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown punctuation.definition.raw.markdown
T 77 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L Users must explicitly exit the loop, otherwise all iterations will be performed.
T 80 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L Users may explicitly return to exit the benchmark immediately.
T 62 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L 
L The `SkipWithError(...)` function may be used at any point within the benchmark,
T 4 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
T 5 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown punctuation.definition.raw.markdown
T 23 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown
T 24 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown punctuation.definition.raw.markdown
T 80 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L including before and after the benchmark loop. Moreover, if `SkipWithError(...)`
T 60 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
T 61 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown punctuation.definition.raw.markdown
T 79 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown
T 80 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown punctuation.definition.raw.markdown
L has been used, it is not required to reach the benchmark loop and one may return
T 80 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L from the benchmark function early.

L The reason the ranged-for loop is faster than using `KeepRunning`, is
T 52 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
T 53 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown punctuation.definition.raw.markdown
T 64 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown
T 65 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown punctuation.definition.raw.markdown
T 69 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L because `KeepRunning` requires a memory load and store of the iteration count
T 8 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
T 9 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown punctuation.definition.raw.markdown
T 20 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown
T 21 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown markup.inline.raw.string.markdown punctuation.definition.raw.markdown
T 77 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L ever iteration, whereas the ranged-for variant is able to keep the iteration count
T 82 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
L in a register.
T 14 text.html.markdown meta.paragraph.markdown
